name: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
title: Local and Air-Gapped Model Deployment
answer: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running AI models on hardware controlled by the law firm or legal department, with no connection to outside networks. This covers document review, summarization, contract clause extraction, e-discovery coding, and internal knowledge retrieval where confidentiality or client consent rules prohibit sending data to third-party cloud services. It also includes models used in litigation support, privilege review, and matter intake workflows. The scope is narrower than general enterprise AI because legal data often includes protected health information, trade secrets, and attorney work product.

sections.body: Local and air-gapped model deployment means running AI models on hardware controlled by the law firm or legal department, with no connection to outside networks. This covers document review, summarization, contract clause extraction, e-discovery coding, and internal knowledge retrieval where confidentiality or client consent rules prohibit sending data to third-party cloud services. It also includes models used in litigation support, privilege review, and matter intake workflows. The scope is narrower than general enterprise AI because legal data often includes protected health information, trade secrets, and attorney work product.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: It typically runs on on-premises servers with one or more GPUs, or on isolated virtual private cloud segments that have no internet egress. Air-gapped deployments add physical or logical network separation, so model weights, inference code, and data all stay inside the boundary. Storage and backup systems must also be inside the boundary, and updates are brought in through controlled media or one-way transfer points. Smaller deployments may run quantized models on a single workstation or a small cluster.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Teams usually start with an open-weight model that is downloaded, scanned, and then moved into the isolated environment. The model is fine-tuned or adapted on internal legal documents, past work product, and matter metadata, often using retrieval augmented generation over a local document index. Prompts and outputs are logged locally for quality control, and lawyers or legal operations staff review model output before it is used in filings or advice. No data leaves the boundary during inference or training.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main rights questions are model license terms, because some open-weight licenses restrict commercial use or require attribution, and the provenance of training data can carry unresolved copyright claims. This site tracks 142 active AI lawsuits, 92 of them intellectual property, which is a reminder that using a model trained on disputed data does not remove underlying IP risk even when deployment is local. Air gapping reduces confidentiality and data breach risk but does not by itself solve accuracy, bias, or privilege waiver problems. Legal teams need an inventory of model version, training data lineage, fine-tuning data, and access logs to respond to discovery or regulatory requests.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Local deployment is moving toward smaller, task-specific models that can run on modest hardware and be updated through controlled channels. More legal departments are pairing air-gapped models with local search indexes and matter management systems so that retrieval and generation happen in one closed loop. Expect stronger procurement language around model provenance, license audits, and on-premises support contracts. The direction is not a single giant model but a set of controlled, auditable models for distinct legal tasks, with clear boundaries between what may be sent to a cloud provider and what must stay inside.
